In this paper, we present a multi-objective low-carbon multimodal transportation planning problem with fuzzy
demand and fuzzy time (MOLCMTPP-FDFT) that minimizes both cost and time while incorporating mandatory
carbon emission, carbon tax, carbon trading, and carbon offset policies. Chance constrained programming and
interval programming are introduced to formulate the fuzzy demand chance constrained programming model
and the fuzzy time interval programming model, respectively. Then, the mathematical model of uncertain
MOLCMTPP-FDFT is transformed into a deterministic model. Based on the sparrow search algorithm, t distri­
bution and the concept of Pareto optimality for multi-objective optimization, we also propose a solution strategy
for the proposed model. In this algorithm, the number of iterations is used as the degree of freedom of - to update
the sparrow location, which strikes a balance between the capabilities of global search and local search. Finally,
the proposed algorithm and MOLCMTPP-FDFT are applied to a real case, resulting in a minimum cost of
260730.48 and a time duration of 13.044, which outperform the minimum cost of 268874.88 and minimum time
of 18.32 obtained using single-mode transportation. The carbon emissions resulting from the lowest-cost solution
obtained using single-mode transportation are 3,198.48, which are signifcantly more than the allowed emis­
sions. Therefore, the proposed algorithm and mathematical model of MOLCMTPP-FDFT are valuable tools for
optimizing multimodal transportation route. Additionally, the experimental results not only validate the superior
effciency and energy-saving benefts of the proposed multimodal transportation routes in comparison to the
actual single-modal transportation, but also demonstrate the applicability of different low-carbon policies.

The competition among logistics enterprises is gradually intensifying
as transportation means continue to improve, and multimodal trans­
portation networks are progressively enhanced. In order to enhance the
core competitiveness of enterprises, it is imperative for them to evaluate
the transportation route scheme based on multiple objectives, including
minimizing transportation cost and time, reducing carbon emissions,
and maximizing customer satisfaction (Adil & Kemal, 2016). Addition­
ally, enterprises should also take into account various uncertain factors
in the transportation system such as advance planning of transport
schemes, seasonal demand fuctuations, and the infuence of human
subjectivity on demand (Zhang, Jin, Yuan, & Zhang, 2021). The trans­
portation process may encounter uncontrollable phenomena and prob­
lems, such as traffc congestion, equipment failure, or extreme weather
conditions. These factors contribute to the unpredictability of trans­
portation time. The decision-makers can effectively design strategies
that are capable of adapting to changes in the external environment,
while minimizing the impact of uncertainties and ensuring the
competitiveness of enterprises. This can be achieved by thoroughly
considering various uncertainties in the external environment and uti­
lizing multiple evaluation indicators as references. The promotion of
low-carbon transportation is effectively achieved through the assess­
ment and formulation of transportation schemes from multiple per­
spectives, even under uncertain conditions (Goncalves, Hsu, & Xu,
2009). Therefore, this paper presents a multi-objective low-carbon
multimodal transportation planning problem with fuzzy demand and
fuzzy time (MOLCMTPP-FDFT), aiming to minimize both transportation
cost and time, while integrating various low-carbon policies into the
model.
In order to fnd a feasible solution for balancing transportation cost,
carbon emissions, and transportation time under different low-carbon
policies. In this paper, a new Pareto-based multi-objective approach is
developed, which combines the sparrow search algorithm (SSA) (Xue, &
Shen, 2020) and t distribution (Kitagawa, 1953) mutation. The proposed
method aims to solve the MOLCMTPP-FDFT and transformation models
considering four low-carbon policies, including mandatory carbon
emission, carbon tax, carbon trading, and carbon offset. There are some
motivations for using the sparrow search algorithm with adaptive t
distribution (ATDSSA) to solve this problem which are as follows.
Firstly, SSA algorithm is a swarm-based metaheuristic method, which
offers several advantages such as minimal parameters, rapid conver­
gence speed, and straightforward implementation. It was primarily
utilized for solving deep learning (Fan et al., 2022), machine learning
(Jia et al., 2022), feature recognition (Wu, Zhang, Han, Nan, & Li, 2022)
and combinatorial optimization problems (Li, & Wang, 2022). It ach­
ieved superior solutions in reasonable computing time (Zhang, Zhang,
Ma, & Liu, 2019). Secondly, the swarm optimization algorithm main­
tains a solution pool during a search process (Zhang, Zhang, Ma, & Liu,
2019; Zhang, Liu, Ma, & Zhang, 2020). Thus, swarm optimization al­
gorithms are particularly suitable for fnding trade-off solutions in a
single run (Zhang, Zhang, Ma, & Liu, 2019; Zhang, Liu, Ma, & Zhang,
2020). Thirdly, metaheuristics are a general algorithmic framework for
fnding solutions to optimization problems, in which local heuristics are
guided and adapted to effciently explore the solution space (Zhang,
Zhang, Ma, & Liu, 2019; Zhang, Liu, Ma, & Zhang, 2020).
The main contributions of this paper are as follows. Firstly, we have
introduced and modeled the MOLCMTPP-FDFT, and transformed model
under different low-carbon policies. This enables us to evaluate the
impact of different low-carbon policies on the multimodal trans­
portation routing scheme. Secondly, in order to obtain high-quality so­
lutions, ATDSSA was designed to solve the MOLCMTPP-FDFT. This
approach not only preserves the characteristics of SSA but also utilizes
the number of iterations as freedom of t distribution for balancing global
and local search abilities, thereby preventing premature convergence or
falling into local optima. Thirdly, chance constrained programming and
interval programming are introduced to address uncertain demand and
time. The multi-objective fuzzy chance constrained programming model
and interval programming model are constructed based on the actual
situation. Furthermore, the proposed ATDSSA incorporates the fast non-
dominated sorting method along with its underlying concept. Finally,
we conduct a comprehensive analysis of the performance of our pro­
posed algorithm. As later reported, our method effciently generates
trade-off solutions for MOLCMTPP-FDFT under different low-carbon
policies.
The rest of this paper is organized as follows. Section 2 provides a
brief overview of the existing literatures. Section 3 formally describes
MOLCMTPP-FDFT and the transformation model under different low-
carbon policies. Section 4 introduces several fuzzy approaches,
including chance constrained programming based on credibility theory,
fuzzy variables, and interval programming. Section 5 presents the
sparrow search algorithm with adaptive t distributed based on non-
dominated sorting method. Section 6 describes computational experi­
ments that analyzed the performance and parameter setting of ATDSSA,
while also applying the proposed MOLCMTPP-FDFT and transformation
models under different low-carbon policies in a real case study. Section 7
summarizes the impact of different low-carbon policies on multimodal
transportation routing decisions.

The aim of this section is to provide a short but comprehensive

Through case analysis, we discussed the infuence of different low-
carbon policies on multimodal transportation routing decisions. These
fndings provide valuable insights for decision-makers involved in
implementing low-carbon multimodal transportation practices and
assist governmental bodies and relevant organizations in formulating
future low-carbon policies.

3. Mathematical model for MOLCMTPP-FDFT
The MOLCMTPP-FDFT refers particularly to the problem of effec­
tively transporting a batch of cargo from the origin to the destination via
a variety of transportation means, such as trucks, ships, trains, and
planes, while taking fuzzy time and demand into account. In this com­
plex transportation system, the effective and rational integration of
various transfer nodes and transportation modes is crucial in minimizing
the transportation time, cost, and carbon emissions that are converted to
costs and associated with low-carbon policies, such as mandatory carbon
emission, carbon tax, carbon trading and carbon compensation.
3.1. The basic MOLCMTPP-FDFT– model I
Logistics enterprise needs to adopt multiple transportation means to
transport some goods with uncertain demand from the origin to the
destination through various transit nodes with the minimum trans­
portation cost and time. In response to national initiatives promoting
low-carbon transportation, these enterprises must develop correspond­
ing schemes for low-carbon transportation under different low-carbon

Besides, scholars have focused on these multimodal transportation
planning problems under uncertainty. Considering the uncertain factors
into multimodal transportation process can reduce the environmental
impacts on the transportation schemes. The multimodal transportation
planning problem under uncertainty mainly includes uncertainties in
transportation time, volume, and customer demand. Uncertain variables
can be classifed into random variables and fuzzy variables (Shi, Bou­
douh, & Grunder, 2017) with different expressions used in routing
optimization problems. Stochastic programming is commonly employed
to solve problems involving random variables, such as robust optimi­
zation (Iyengar, 2005) and auxiliary variable method (Bertsimas, & Sim,
2004). Triangular fuzzy numbers, trapezoidal fuzzy numbers and in­
terval numbers are typically utilized to represent fuzzy variables.
Furthermore, expected value models (Xu, Yan, & Li, 2011), chance
constrained programming (Messaoud, 2021), and interval programming
(Subulan, 2020; Robers, & Ben-Israel, 1969) are applied to transform
fuzzy variables into certain ones.
Kalinina, Olsson and Larsson (2013) used a fuzzy chance constraint
model to solve the multimodal transportation with uncertain time.
Fazayeli, Eydi and Kamalabadi (2018) proposed a mixed integer math­
ematical fuzzy model for the multimodal transportation planning
problem with fuzzy demand. A fuzzy
\upalpha
-cut technology is used to trans­
form the fuzzy demand an expectation interval, and transformed the
original fuzzy model into an auxiliary deterministic one. Zhang (2022)
considered the optimization of multimodal transportation routing under
the double uncertainty in both time window and demand by using
trapezoidal fuzzy variables to represent these uncertainties. The fuzzy
chance constrained programming was applied to solve the bi-objective
fuzzy model. (Zhang, 2022).
The research on MOLCMTPP-FDFT under different low-carbon pol­
icies is limited, highlighting the need for extensive investigation in this
area. This includes employing hybrid methods that utilize various heu­
ristic evolutionary/swarm algorithms, exact methods, and local search
techniques to enhance solution quality and/or reduce computational
time (Zhang, Zhang, Ma, & Liu, 2019; Zhang, Liu, Ma, & Zhang, 2020).
In this paper, we aim to construct MOLCMTPP-FDFT under various low-
carbon policies such as mandatory carbon emission, carbon tax, carbon
trading and carbon offset. To address these problems, we propose
Pareto-based sparrow search algorithm with adaptive t distributed.
Through case analysis, we discussed the infuence of different low-
carbon policies on multimodal transportation routing decisions. These
fndings provide valuable insights for decision-makers involved in
implementing low-carbon multimodal transportation practices and
assist governmental bodies and relevant organizations in formulating
future low-carbon policies.
Finally, Table 1 classifes and summarizes literature mentioned
above from the aspects of problem categories, uncertainty components
of problems, transportation mode, optimization objectives, carbon
emissions, low-carbon policies and solution methodology (Subulan,
2020). As shown in Table 1, the literature on multimodal transportation
planning problem is abundant. However, there remains a scarcity of
studies that consider multiple objectives, various uncertainties, and
multiple low-carbon policies. Most of existing literature have concen­
trated on transportation in deterministic environments or have only
taken one uncertain factor into account. They have also neglected low-
carbon policies when estimating carbon emissions, which makes them
inaccurate representations of reality. When solving the low-carbon
multimodal transportation planning problem, various uncertain fac­
tors and multiple low-carbon policies need to be considered simulta­
neously in order to accurately refect reality.
3. Mathematical model for MOLCMTPP-FDFT
The MOLCMTPP-FDFT refers particularly to the problem of effec­
tively transporting a batch of cargo from the origin to the destination via
a variety of transportation means, such as trucks, ships, trains, and
planes, while taking fuzzy time and demand into account. In this com­
plex transportation system, the effective and rational integration of
various transfer nodes and transportation modes is crucial in minimizing
the transportation time, cost, and carbon emissions that are converted to
costs and associated with low-carbon policies, such as mandatory carbon
emission, carbon tax, carbon trading and carbon compensation.
3.1. The basic MOLCMTPP-FDFT– model I
Logistics enterprise needs to adopt multiple transportation means to
transport some goods with uncertain demand from the origin to the
destination through various transit nodes with the minimum trans­
portation cost and time. In response to national initiatives promoting
low-carbon transportation, these enterprises must develop correspond­
ing schemes for low-carbon transportation under different low-carbon
policies. To facilitate model construction, we make the following as­
sumptions: (1) goods cannot be disassembled in transportation process;
(2) selecting at most one transportation mode between two transit
nodes; (3) each transit node can only carry out mode conversion at most
once; (4) capacity constraint should be considered for each trans­
portation section and transit node; (5) external factors such as weather
conditions, equipment failure or cargo damage are not taken into
account.

4. The fuzzy approach
Currently, stochastic programming, fuzzy programming and interval
programming are commonly used to deal with uncertain parameters in
routing optimization. Interval programming belongs to the category of
fuzzy programming. In generally, less data can be used to evaluate the
probability distribution of demand for the decision makers, resulting in a
less feasible stochastic programming. Existing literature commonly
employs triangular fuzzy variables, trapezoidal fuzzy variables, and in­
terval numbers as methods to represent those uncertain variables. The
maximum membership degree of triangular fuzzy numbers can only
correspond to one value, which is only applicable to a clearly defned
range. In contrast, trapezoidal fuzzy numbers are more fexible, and the
maximum membership degree of trapezoidal fuzzy numbers can corre­
spond to an interval, which allows different decision makers to hold
varying opinions on the most likely value. Some scholars have proposed
that the trapezoidal fuzzy numbers can better represent the fuzzy de­
mand in actual situation. In addition, weather, road conditions and
personnel habits all impact transportation time. It is possible to roughly
determine the time range for each road section and transit node based on
past experience and recent road conditions. Therefore, the fexible
trapezoidal fuzzy number is used to represent fuzzy demand while using
interval numbers for dealing fuzzy time.

spans.content: 7. Conclusion
The mathematical models are developed for multimodal trans­
portation planning problem with fuzzy demand and fuzzy time under
different carbon emission policies, aiming to minimize both cost and
time of low-carbon transportation. It is possible to provide more
economical and environmentally friendly transportation selections for
the multimodal transportation routing problem under different low-
carbon policies by incorporating unpredictable factors and the impact of
transport and transit capacities. Furthermore, the original SSA has been
improved to solve the MOLCMTPP-FDFT by utilizing the number of it­
erations as a degree of freedom for t distribution, which effectively
balances local and global search capabilities of the SSA and compensates
for its susceptibility to local optima. The experimental results demon­
strate that mandatory carbon emission and carbon tax policies can
successfully reduce carbon emissions, which provides appropriate ap­
proaches for urgent reduction in carbon emissions. The implementation
of carbon trading policy can partially alleviate enterprise costs, thereby
facilitating the early-stage promotion of low-carbon transportation
practices.
ATDSSA has also been compared with other state-of-the-art intelli­
gent optimization algorithms, such as GWO, PSO and NSGA-II. Although
ATDSSA and NSGA-II obtain the same non-dominated solutions, the
computation time required by ATDSSA is shorter than that of GSA, PSO
and NSGA-II. Therefore, we can conclude that the proposed ATDSSA is a
very competitive algorithm for solving multi-objective optimization
problems. It can also be used to solve other multi-objective combina­
torial optimization problems, such as multi-objective location routing
problem, multi-objective vehicle routing problem, and multi-objective
facility location problem. Additionally, the proposed mathematical
model of MOLCMTPP-FDFT can obtain reasonable transportation routes
while ensuring the minimization of cost, carbon emission and trans­
portation time, which is helpful to the promotion of low-carbon trans­
portation network.
The ATDSSA is a competitive algorithm that can effectively solve not
only the multi-objective multimodal transportation planning problems,
but also vehicle routing problem, location-routing problem and other
combinatorial optimization problems. The mathematical model of
MOLCMTPP-FDFT can provide cost-effective, environmentally-friendly
and effcient transportation solution for logistics. However, this study
also has two primary limitations. Firstly, due to the limited scope of this
paper, a theoretical analysis of the convergence of ATDSS was not
conducted. Secondly, there are many uncertainties in realistic trans­
portation networks, but this study only considers fuzzy demand and
time.
To extend this work and overcome its limitations, the following
works can be done in the future:(1) exploring some effective methods to
balance the global search and local search to further improve the per­
formance of the algorithm. (2) proposing other methods to deal with
uncertain variables, and reducing the impact of environmental changes
on routing decision. (3) considering the low-carbon multimodal trans­
portation of special products such as dangerous products, emergency
supplies, and perishable food.
